searchText: halo eth2 https://twitter.com/etherchain_org/status/1336949569498853377 it's here 🙏 <@!340345049063882753> <@!203220829473996800> <@!476250636548308992> still not enough data but it is starting to appear as a pattern that the Teku's improvements even though haven't reduced the minimal delay on slot 0, they have substantially reduced the maximum delay compared to the baseline on pyrmont. Still it is interesting to note that on slot 0, Teku's nodes are consistently above the 2 second mark, while baseline has a lot of points below this. That's about 10K points total, will need an extra couple of days to confirm, but it looks that this is actually the case For example I cannot distiguish EF Teku's from the newer commits, therefore it looks like the newer improvements didn't do much with respect to this issue Ok, Perhaps all this data is skewed a lot by Nimbus, all the long points on slot 0 and 1 correspond to Nimbus nodes I better post on the pyrmont channel I was planning to try out some improvements on prylabs side, but havent had the time. It should have allowed us to process slot 0 faster in the gossip layer Unfortunately I don't have prysm points in the last couple of days (I am filtering by graffiti and don't see any from you. I know <@!203220829473996800>'s prysm nodes are down. But it seems that essentially all of the points above 4 seconds are Nimbus on the first two slots and interestingly enough all of the points below 2 seconds are also Nimbus Yes, been having some issues with Prysm io work during attestations being published. Prysm team is working on improvements there There are many things that I am taking out of the per-client graph: all of lighthouse blocks are after 2 seconds, at all slots sorry after 1 second But this may be a skew on my node that is prysm, so this is measuring the delay that those blocks are taking to get to my node I'd like to see if someone on lighthouse can carry the same analysis and report something different, cause that would point to network topology more than client performance, or at least rule this out <@755590043632140352> are you computing time based on genesis time, or minimum genesis time? There's a small difference that might offset things actual genesis time it was 7 seconds after if I remember correctly `genesis_testnet = 1605700807` Yep, 7 for Pyrmont, 23 for mainnet But also if you look at the graph I posted on the pyrmont channel, it's insteresting the Lighthouse clustering and Teku's outperforming in that measure at other slots Interesting, sorry I didn't have time to look deeper into this yet
